1) we describe a new approach to compositional generalization that does not rely on latent symbolic structure and 2) we demonstrate that this approach significantly improves generalization performance on two language processing problems.

1) a simple learned data augmentation scheme can enable compositional generalization in neural sequence models; 2) this augmentation is effective in settings where it enables learning of new construction or tenses from as little as eight examples; and 3) the augmentation can be used in conjunction with other techniques to improve performance in settings where it is not sufficient on its own.

we describe an approach to data augmentation that improves generalization of neural sequence models on compositional tasks and that we show this approach can be applied to a wide range of tasks, including instruction following and morphological analysis.

the question: How can we learn to recombine and resample training data to improve generalization in sequence models?
how to make neural sequence models more robust to compositional generalization, a problem of great importance in natural language processing.

R&R is an effective method to augment data and enable neural sequence models to learn new constructions and tences from few initial examples.

R&R enables neural sequence models to learn new constructions and tences with as little as 8 examples, and significantly improves generalization on two language processing problems: instruction following (SCAN) where it learns new constructions and SIGMORPHON where it learns new tenses.
the R&R approach is able to significantly improve the generalization of a large class of compositional generalization tasks, without the need for symbolic scaffolds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to learn a compositional language from a small number of examples.
we propose a data augmentation scheme, called R&R, that allows a category of compositional inductive biases to be learned from data alone.

we have developed a simple, effective, and general data augmentation scheme for compositional generalization, and that this approach can be applied to any neural sequence model without any additional architectural changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural models can be made more robust in compositional generalization settings by learning to augment their own training data.
a simple, data-driven approach can enable a neural model to learn a wide range of compositional generalization tasks without the need for explicit symbolic structure or supervision.

a simple, data-driven augmentation scheme can improve the generalization capabilities of a standard neural sequence model, and that such an augmentation scheme is not only feasible but can be trained on the fly, without any additional data or computational overhead.
